## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Ūnapañcabandhana Sikkhāpada* (Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 22) governs the repair and replacement of an almsbowl [Hirakawa 1982]. Under this rule, a monk commits an offense requiring forfeiture (*nissaggiya*) and confession (*pācittiya*) if he requests a new bowl when his existing bowl is still usable, specifically if it has been broken or mended in fewer than five places; if broken in more than five places, an exchange is permitted [Hirakawa 1982]. The text has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

Textual reuse data compiled by DharmaNexus demonstrates extensive formulaic overlap with other Vinaya texts. Within the Pali Canon, substantial passages are shared with Khandhaka chapters—most notably the *Senāsanakkhandhaka* (Kd 16), *Cīvarakkhandhaka* (Kd 8), *Samathakkhandhaka* (Kd 14), and *Khuddakavatthukkhandhaka* (Kd 15)—as well as other Vibhaṅga rules (including Np 19, Np 7, and Pc 86) and late manuals such as the *Vinayasaṅgaha-aṭṭhakathā* and *Vinayālaṅkāra-ṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns the rule with Tibetan translations of Vinaya treatises, including the *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003), the *Pratimokṣasūtraṭīkā Vinayasamuccaya* (D4106), and the *Vinayasaṃgraha* (D4105) [DharmaNexus].
